summary: Gives the reasoning for moving RIP version 1 to historic status. The main reason is its classful nature, meaning it carries no subnet mask information. It is informational.

eli5.summary: An old map that only showed whole towns and could not show smaller neighborhoods. This note explains why that map was retired.

subtitle: Why RIP version 1 became obsolete for modern networks

tldr.problem: RIPv1 worked for early, simple networks but became inadequate as the Internet grew more complex with subnets, CIDR supernetting, and variable-length subnet masks.
tldr.mechanism: RIPv1 carries no subnet mask information in its packets; it infers the prefix length directly from the address class, assuming all subnets use the same mask. It also limits routing distance to 16 hops and struggles with routing protocol coexistence.
tldr.outcome: RIPv1 was declared Historic in favor of RIPv2, which carries mask information and supports modern address allocation.

today: RFC 1923 is an Informational applicability statement. RIPv1 itself is Historic; this memo explains why.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content:
RIPv1 was one of the first dynamic routing protocols in the Internet and worked well for simple topologies in the early days. However, the Internet evolved. The introduction of subnets (dividing a network address into smaller segments) and CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) fundamentally changed how addresses are allocated. RIPv1, a classful protocol, could not evolve to support this.

While RIPv1 remains in use in private networks, it is no longer applicable to the global Internet.
sections.eli5: RIP version 1 was made before networks were divided into small pieces. When that became necessary, the old version stopped working well.

sections.title: RIPv1's Fatal Limitations
sections.content:
Classfulness: RIPv1 packets contain no subnet mask. For remote addresses, it assumes the classful prefix (24 bits for a Class C address). This breaks with variable-length subnetting, CIDR supernetting, and mixed-mask topologies. If a network using RIPv1 connects to a network using modern routing, RIPv1 will corrupt mask information as it passes through.

Distance vector limits: RIPv1 uses hop count as its metric, with a maximum of 16 hops before a route is considered unreachable. Networks larger than 16 hops cannot use RIPv1. Additionally, the protocol must count to infinity to purge bad routes, slowing convergence when topology changes.
sections.eli5: RIPv1 could not understand neighborhoods of different sizes, and it could not reach farther than 16 steps away.

sections.title: What to Use Instead
sections.content:
RIPv2, defined in RFC 1723, fixes the mask problem by including subnet mask information in each routing advertisement. For any network that needs dynamic routing, RIPv2 is the recommended replacement.

RIPv1 may still be used in simple private networks with fixed (non-variable) subnetting, where either a default route handles external traffic or the network is isolated from the Internet. It is not acceptable for global Internet routing or mixed-mask environments.
sections.eli5: Use RIP version 2 instead, or use a more modern routing protocol if you need to.
